goal: Runner step sessions on claude can run on the Max plan's monthly API credit instead of the plan's weekly and 5-hour budget. Martin picks the mode with `mc run --billing plan|credits|auto`: `plan` is today's behaviour, `credits` runs every new claude step session on the API key, and `auto` moves to the key when the last seen seven-day utilization is at or above 80 % (`CREDITS_AT_UTILIZATION`) or when the plan has refused a session, and back to the plan after the plan's reset.

A refusal no longer only sleeps: in `auto` a plan refusal hands the step to the credit, and an exhausted or rejected credit hands it back to the plan. Which billing a session ran on is in the register, on the page and in `mc step`.
contract: The default mode is `plan`. An absent, unreadable or unknown `~/mc/runner/billing.json` reads as `plan`, and nothing in this project changes what a runner does until Martin runs `mc run --billing credits` or `mc run --billing auto`.

The one exception to the stance in `src/adapters/claude-code.js` (the comment above `tokenLocations`, ~line 303–316: mc never turns a vault secret into an environment variable) is this, and only this: the value of the vault record labelled `mc-api-key`, as `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, in the environment of a claude session that `runStep` (`src/mc/run.js`) launches for a step, when the billing chosen for that launch is `credits`. The comment is updated to name the exception and the step-credits ruling.

The key is visible to every command the credits session runs (its Bash tool inherits the environment: tests, `mc merge`, a dev server). Martin accepted this on 2026-10-11 (ruling 38); the Console spend cap on the `mc` workspace is the bound. No step scrubs it from children or routes it through `apiKeyHelper`, which would expose it the same way.

The label is a constant in the module that reads it, with no label, path, destination or environment parameter, in the shape of `src/vault/engine/c1-claude-lease.js`. `mc vault get` stays disabled (`cmdGet`, `src/cli/vault.js:877`); no verb prints, exports or writes the key; the key is never logged, never written to a file, never put in `current` files, the register, runs.tsv or a say line, and is not held beyond the launch that uses it.

A session whose billing is `plan` gets no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and no `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` in its environment, even when the runner's own environment has one: billing follows the mode and nothing else.
Billing is chosen at a session boundary only: a new step session, a resume after an interruption, or a fresh session after one. A running session keeps the billing it started with.
A step session on credits runs with the same tool, model, effort and advisor the plan names (`sessionSettings`, `src/mc/run-plan.js`). The credit changes who pays, not how the step runs.
A resume across a billing change counts as cold: `recoveryFor` (`src/mc/run-plan.js:995`) never calls it warm, and the cold rule (`COLD_RESUME_MAX_TOKENS`) decides resume or fresh.
codex sessions, `mc helper --intake`, and every interactive session (`mc brief`, `mc plan`, `mc work`, `mc worker`) are untouched: they never get the key and never read the billing mode.

Thresholds are exported constants with a comment saying why, not settings: `CREDITS_AT_UTILIZATION` = 0.8 (the last fifth of the weekly budget is left for Martin's own interactive work, which the credit does not cover), `CREDITS_RETRY_MS` = 24 h.
Every step runs `npm test` and lands through `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`.
out_of_scope: The Console side: the `mc` workspace, its spend limit, auto-reload, buying credits, creating the key. Those are Martin's.
Asking Anthropic for the credit balance or the next grant date. There is no endpoint for it with a normal key; an exhausted credit is learned from the refusal.
memoro me's own use of the credit (batch jobs, photo analysis).
A new column in `~/mc/runner/log/runs.tsv` (`RUNS_HEADER` is pinned by `tests/mc/run-doc.test.js`); billing is in the register and the say lines.
Fixing the vault key cache or the Memoro re-login: that is project `vault-repair`, which this plan waits for.

steps.title: 1. The billing mode and the plan's windows: `mc run --billing`, `billing.json`, `billing-state.json`
steps.done_when: `mc run --billing [plan|credits|auto]` reads and writes `~/mc/runner/billing.json`, the runner records the 5-hour and seven-day windows from every claude plan session's stream into `~/mc/runner/billing-state.json`, `billingFor` answers which billing a launch would get, no session is launched differently yet, and `npm test` is green.
instruction: New module `src/mc/billing.js`, modelled on `src/mc/lane-count.js` (read never throws, a broken file is the default, writes with `writeJsonAtomic` from `src/mc/atomic-write.js`, mode 0600). Paths under `runnerDir()` (`src/mc/paths.js:107`): `billingPath()` → `billing.json`, `billingStatePath()` → `billing-state.json`. Exports: `BILLING_MODES = ['plan','credits','auto']`, `DEFAULT_BILLING = 'plan'`, `CREDITS_AT_UTILIZATION = 0.8`, `CREDITS_RETRY_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000`, each constant with a comment saying why (contract).

`billing.json` is Martin's: `{ "mode": "plan"|"credits"|"auto", "set": <iso> }`. `readBillingMode({ root })` returns the mode, `plan` for anything absent, unparsable or unknown. `writeBillingMode(value, { root, now })` refuses anything not in `BILLING_MODES` with `{ ok: false, reason }` naming the three, otherwise writes the file and also clears `credits.unusable_until` and `credits.why` in the state file (Martin setting the mode is his word that the key or the balance was fixed), returning `{ ok: true, mode }`.

`billing-state.json` is the runner's: `{ "plan": { "five_hour": { "utilization": <0..1>, "resets_at": <iso> } | null, "seven_day": { … } | null, "seen": <iso> | null, "refused_until": <iso> | null }, "credits": { "unusable_until": <iso> | null, "why": <string> | null } }`. `readBillingState({ root })` normalises (any bad field → null) and never throws; `patchBillingState(patch, { root })` reads, merges per top-level key, writes whole.

`planWindows(stdout)`: the last `rate_limit_event` in a claude stream-json run that carries `rate_limit_info.unifiedWindows`, as `{ five_hour, seven_day }` with `resets_at` converted from epoch seconds to ISO; null when there is none. The shape, from `~/mc/runner/log/*.jsonl` on 2026-10-11: `{"type":"rate_limit_event","rate_limit_info":{"status":"allowed_warning","resetsAt":1792155600,"rateLimitType":"seven_day","utilization":0.59,…,"unifiedWindows":{"five_hour":{"utilization":0.08,"resetsAt":1791721200},"seven_day":{"utilization":0.59,"resetsAt":1792155600}}}}`. Parse line by line the way `streamRateLimit` does (`src/mc/run-plan.js` ~1340); a window whose numbers are not finite is null.

`billingFor({ mode, state, toolId, now })` → `{ billing: 'plan'|'credits', why }`, pure. In order: `toolId !== 'claude-code'` → plan (`why`: the tool); `state.credits.unusable_until` after `now` → plan (why names `credits.why` and the time); mode `plan` → plan; mode `credits` → credits; mode `auto`: `state.plan.refused_until` after `now` → credits; `seven_day.utilization >= CREDITS_AT_UTILIZATION` and its `resets_at` after `now` → credits (why: `seven-day 83 %, resets <iso>`); otherwise plan. A seven-day window whose reset has passed is stale and counts as unknown, which is plan: that is the way back.

Runner recording (`src/mc/run.js`, `runStep`): after the session loop ends (after `writeSessionLogs(out, result)`, ~line 2233), when `launch.id === 'claude-code'`, call `planWindows(result.stdout)` and, when it is not null, `patchBillingState({ plan: { five_hour, seven_day, seen: stamp() } })`. Take the file through a `deps.billing` object in `realDeps` (`readMode`, `readState`, `patchState`) so tests stub it; lanes share one process, so a write is the whole file and the last write wins. Nothing else in `runStep` changes in this step.

`mc run --billing` (`src/mc/commands/run.js`): parse it in `parseRunArgs` beside `--update` (~line 239) as an order on its own: `mc run --billing` prints, `mc run --billing <mode>` writes then prints; `mc run billing [<mode>]` is the same, as `update` is. Any other flag with it is an error, like `--update`'s. Add `if (opts.verb === 'billing') return billing(opts, deps)` to `order` and a `billing()` beside `lanes()` returning `{ ok, code, lines }`. Lines: `billing <mode>` (and `— set <iso>` when written); `plan: 5-hour <n> % (resets <local time>) · seven-day <n> % (resets <local time>) · seen <age>` or `plan: no window seen yet`; `plan refused until <time>` when set and in the future; `credits unusable until <time> — <why>` when set and in the future; `next claude step session: <plan|credits> — <why>` from `billingFor` with `toolId: 'claude-code'`. When writing, add `read at the next session — no restart needed`. Add the form to `USAGE` and to the `mc run` block of `src/mc/help-text.js`.

Docs: `docs/technical/mc-run.md` gets a section `### Billing` stating the three modes, the files, that `auto` moves at 80 % of the seven-day window, that the mode is read at every new session, and that this step only records. Pin the 80 in `tests/mc/run-doc.test.js` the way the quota sleep is pinned (read the number from the doc, compare with `CREDITS_AT_UTILIZATION * 100`).

Tests: `tests/mc/billing.test.js` (read/write/normalise, `planWindows` on the shape above, on a stream without `unifiedWindows` and on a broken line; `billingFor` cases listed in the success criteria) and `tests/mc/commands/run-billing.test.js` modelled on `tests/mc/commands/run-lanes.test.js` (parse, refusal of an unknown mode with exit 2, printed lines, the write clearing the credit mark). In `tests/mc/run.test.js` add one case: a claude session whose stream carries the event above patches the state with `seven_day.utilization` 0.59. `npm test` green.

steps.title: 2. The key, read from the vault for one purpose: `readStepCreditKey`
steps.done_when: `src/vault/engine/step-credit-key.js` exports `readStepCreditKey()` that returns `{ ok: true, key }` for the single vault record labelled `mc-api-key` using only the cached vault key, or `{ ok: false, reason }`, with no parameter that names a label, path or destination; the claude-code adapter's stance comment names the exception; tests cover envelope and legacy rows; `npm test` is green.
instruction: Model the module on `src/vault/engine/c1-claude-lease.js` (`runC1ClaudeVaultLeaseCore` and `runC1ClaudeVaultLeaseWithCache`, ~lines 135–191), which reads one fixed record with the cached vault key. `export const STEP_CREDIT_KEY_LABEL = 'mc-api-key'`. `export async function readStepCreditKey({ deps = {} } = {})`: `deps` holds only test seams (`readCachedVaultKey`, `portal`, `api`), never a label.

Order: `readCachedVaultKey()` (`src/vault/engine/key-cache.js`) → none is `{ ok: false, reason: 'vault-locked' }` (the reason Martin reads; the fix is `mc vault unlock` in a terminal). Portal: the Memoro token from the keychain account `memoro-api-token` and `readConfig().apiUrl`, as `resolveTrustedPortal` does (~line 193); none is `{ ok: false, reason: 'not-logged-in' }`. When the cache carries `authHash`, `VaultApi.unlockVault(portal, { authHash, deviceId })` first, as the lease does; a refusal is `{ ok: false, reason: 'vault-refused' }`. `VaultApi.getStatus` and, when `wrapped_crk` and `crk_iv` are present, `unwrapCustodyRoot(cache.vaultKey, …)` (`src/vault/engine/custody-crypto.js`).

`VaultApi.listSecrets(portal)`; for each row: envelope rows (`isEnvelopeSecret`, custody-crypto.js:232) of class `secret` → `decryptEnvelopeLabel(crk, row)`; legacy rows → `decryptSecret(vaultKey, row.encrypted_label, row.label_iv)` (`src/vault/engine/client-crypto.js:187`). Keep the rows whose label equals the constant. Zero is `{ ok: false, reason: 'no-key' }`, more than one is `{ ok: false, reason: 'key-ambiguous' }`. Decrypt the one: `decryptEnvelopeSecret(crk, row)` or `decryptSecretPayload(vaultKey, row)` (client-crypto.js:215); the payload is what `mc vault set` writes (`buildSecretPayload`, `src/vault/engine/types.js:56`: `{ kind, token, … }`). Accept `kind` `api_token` with a non-empty string `token` without whitespace or line breaks; anything else is `{ ok: false, reason: 'key-unreadable' }`.

Zero the vault key bytes in a `finally` (`cache.vaultKeyBytes?.fill?.(0)`), as the lease does. Every failure path returns, never throws, and no return value, error message or log line contains the key or any decrypted label other than the constant.

`src/adapters/claude-code.js`: the comment block above `tokenLocations` (~303–316) keeps its stance and adds one paragraph: the single exception is `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from the vault label `mc-api-key` (`readStepCreditKey`), for runner step sessions whose billing is `credits`, under the step-credits ruling. No code in the adapter changes.

Tests: `tests/vault/engine/step-credit-key.test.js` with `createMockVaultServer` and `makeTestPortal` (`tests/vault/engine/_helpers/mock-server.js`) and the fixtures the c1 lease and vault-command tests use: the key found in an envelope row and in a legacy row; `no-key`, `key-ambiguous`, `vault-locked` (cache stub returns null), `key-unreadable` (payload kind `oauth_token`); the function's `length` and its accepted `deps` keys show no label parameter; the key never appears in a `reason`. `tests/architecture/layer-boundaries.test.js` must stay green (the new module is in the `vault` layer and imports only `vault` and `lib`). `npm test` green.

steps.title: 3. A claude step session runs on the billing `billingFor` gives it
steps.done_when: Every claude step session `runStep` launches is started on the billing `billingFor` returns for that launch — with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from `readStepCreditKey` on credits, and with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` removed on plan — the register, the current file, the page and `mc step` show it, and `npm test` is green.
instruction: `streamSession` (`src/mc/run.js:259`) and `realDeps().session` (~line 508–511): add an `unsetEnv` option, an array of names deleted from the merged environment after `{ ...env, BASH_…, ...options.env }` is built. Nothing else in the merge changes.

In `runStep`, `launchOnce` (~line 2176) chooses billing per launch, not once per step: `const choice = billingFor({ mode: deps.billing.readMode(), state: deps.billing.readState(), toolId: launch.id, now: deps.now() })`. When `choice.billing === 'credits'`, `const got = await deps.creditKey()` (`realDeps`: `readStepCreditKey`); on `{ ok: false }` the launch is plan and a say line says `credits wanted (<why>) but the key could not be read (<reason>) — plan`. Credits: `env` gets `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: got.key`; plan: `unsetEnv: ['ANTHROPIC_API_KEY', 'ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN']`. Drop the reference to the key as soon as `deps.session` has been called. codex launches never call `deps.creditKey` (`billingFor` already answers plan for them).

Record the billing: the `session` objects written by `recordStep` at the start (~line 2156) and in `onSpawn` (~line 2193) get `billing`; the lane's `current` object (~line 2128) gets `billing`; the starting say line (~line 2116) gets `· on credits (<why>)` when it is credits. On a resume inside the loop the launch chooses again and `recordStep` updates `session.billing`.

Check what claude says it used: the first `{"type":"system","subtype":"init"}` line of the stream carries `apiKeySource` — `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` when the env key was used (measured 2026-10-11 with claude 2.1.296: `apiKeySource: 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'`, and a warning that the env key takes precedence over the claude.ai login). After the session, when the billing was credits and `apiKeySource` is not `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or plan and it is, say `<name>: session ran on <apiKeySource>, not <billing>`. Add `apiKeySource` to what `streamSummary` or `sessionStanding` (`src/mc/run-plan.js`) reads, whichever already walks the init line; if neither does, a small `initSource(stdout)` beside `streamRateLimit`.

`recordInterrupted` (`src/mc/run.js:639`) takes `billing` and writes it into the `interrupted` record; the call in `sweepRunning` (~line 752) passes `session.billing ?? 'plan'`, the one after the session (~line 2331) passes the billing of the last launch.

Show it: `src/mc/status-collect.js` (~line 306) adds `billing: current.billing || null` to the lane item; `src/mc/page-render.js` (~line 688) adds `credits` to the grey tool/model text when `item.billing === 'credits'` and nothing when it is `plan` or null. `src/mc/commands/step.js` `entryLines` (~line 237): a running step whose `session.billing` is `credits` gets the bit `on credits`; `interruptedLine` (~line 222) adds `on credits` when the record's billing is credits.

Tests in `tests/mc/run.test.js` with `deps.billing` and `deps.creditKey` stubbed and `deps.session` capturing its options: mode `credits` → `env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is the stub key, register `session.billing === 'credits'`, current file `billing: 'credits'`; mode `plan` → `unsetEnv` holds both names and no key in `env`; mode `credits` with `creditKey` returning `{ ok: false, reason: 'vault-locked' }` → plan and the say line; a codex plan in mode `credits` → `creditKey` never called. `tests/mc/page.test.js` and `tests/mc/commands/step.test.js` for the display. `npm test` green.

steps.title: 4. Refusals hand the step over instead of sleeping
steps.done_when: In `auto`, a plan refusal writes `plan.refused_until` and hands the step to the next pick on credits without a quota sleep; on any mode, an exhausted or rejected credit writes `credits.unusable_until` (now + 24 h) and hands the step back to the plan; a hand-over is an `interrupted` record that does not count towards `INTERRUPT_LIMIT`; a resume across billings is never warm; `npm test` is green.
instruction: `apiInterruption` (`src/mc/run-plan.js` ~line 1360): before the quota test, `/credit balance is too low/iu` → `{ kind: 'credits', said }` and `/invalid api key/iu` → `{ kind: 'key', said }`. The texts: `Your credit balance is too low to access the Anthropic API. Please go to Plans & Billing to upgrade or purchase credits.` (Anthropic's docs for exhausted credits) and `Invalid API key · Fix external API key` (measured 2026-10-11: `terminal_reason: 'api_error'`, `subtype: 'success'`, exit 1). `readSessionOutput` already passes `interrupted.kind` through (~line 1300); `note` for these two is `interrupted`.

Plan refusals are written down: wherever the runner learns a plan session was refused — `last.interrupted === 'quota'` in the resume loop (~line 2215) and `read.quota` after the session (~line 2316, 2345) — and the session's billing was `plan`, `patchBillingState({ plan: { refused_until } })` with the refusal's reset (`last.quotaReset` / `read.quotaReset`) or, when it named none, now + `QUOTA_SLEEP_MS`. A refusal on a credits session (429 from the API's own rate limit) does not touch `plan` and is handled exactly as today.

Credit failures are written down: `last.interrupted` or `read.interrupted` `credits` or `key` on a credits session → `patchBillingState({ credits: { unusable_until: now + CREDITS_RETRY_MS, why: 'credit balance too low' | 'API key rejected' } })` and a say line naming it and `mc run --billing <mode>` as the way to clear it early.

Hand-over instead of sleeping: in the resume loop, after writing the state, ask `billingFor` for the next launch. When it differs from the billing the session ran on, `break` without `quotaPause` and without resuming, and remember `handOver = { from, to }`. After the loop, in the outcome chain (~line 2290–2338), put a branch before `else if (read.quota)`: when `handOver` is set and no earlier branch matched (the register still says `running`), call `recordInterrupted({ …, billing: from, counted: false })` and set `note` to `${note},handed-to-<to>`; skip the trailing `if (read.quota && !waited) await quotaPause(...)` when `handOver` is set. When `billingFor` gives the same billing (mode `plan`, or the other side unusable too), everything behaves as today: quota sleeps, server errors retry, and a credit failure with the plan refused falls through to the existing branches.
`recordInterrupted` gains `counted = true`: when false, `count` stays `was?.interrupted?.count || 0` and the `INTERRUPT_LIMIT` branch is not taken — a hand-over is not a death.

`recoveryFor` (`src/mc/run-plan.js:995`) gains `billingNow`: when `(record.billing || 'plan') !== billingNow`, skip the warm branch and prefix the cold reasons with `billing changed <from>→<to>, `. `recoveryOf` (`src/mc/run.js` ~line 669) passes `billingFor({ mode, state, toolId: <the plan's tool as launch id>, now }).billing`. The prompt cache is per organisation and workspace, so a session moving between the plan's login and the key's workspace never finds its cache.

Tests: `tests/mc/run-plan.test.js` — the two texts give `credits` and `key`; a quota text still gives `quota`; `recoveryFor` with `billing: 'plan'`, `billingNow: 'credits'` and a last activity one minute ago is `resume` only when the tokens are under `COLD_RESUME_MAX_TOKENS` and `fresh` above, never `warm`. `tests/mc/run.test.js` — mode `auto`, a claude session ending in a 429 refusal: `refused_until` written, `deps.sleep` not called for a quota pause, the step `ready` with `interrupted.billing: 'plan'` and `count` unchanged, note `…,handed-to-credits`; mode `credits`, a session ending `Your credit balance is too low…`: `credits.unusable_until` ≈ now + 24 h, the step handed to plan; mode `plan`, the same 429: today's quota pause, unchanged. Update `docs/technical/mc-run.md § Billing` with the hand-over and the 24 h mark. `npm test` green.
